newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks limp up at open after Dow record.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks limp up at open after Dow record.

text.p: Australian stocks made a slow but solid start on Tuesday despite a new record high on Wall Street, as investors again showed reluctance to buy ahead of next week's Australian budget.
The All Ordinaries index was 11.6 points higher at 2,504.3, just off its morning high of 2,508.1.
Brokers said they had expected the market to open a lot stronger given the record breaking run in New York, adding that the local bourse recent had moved independent of the Dow.

"I think the market should have been up a lot stronger and it's not, because people look like they are sitting on their hands until more data comes out next week," said David Hassett, a broker at Hartley Poynton.
It is the second day in a row brokers had expected surges on Wall Street to carry the local bourse to test new record levels, which were set last week.
Brokers said there were little signs of a fallout among junior gold stocks following the Busang/Bre-X gold debacle, which has become the biggest gold fraud in history.
Shares in junior miner Golden Valley, which has a disputed claim on part of the Busang project, continued to fall.
However, the Australian gold sector reversed most of the losses its made on Monday after the Bre-X announcement.
Upmarket retailer David Jones shares were mildly positive despite reporting before the market opening lower third quarter sales and a continuation of slow trading conditions.
